title: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport / Massimiliano & Doriana Fuksas
summary_en: Terminal 3 of Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport is a roughly 500,000 m² terminal conceived as an aerodynamic tunnel evoking a manta ray. The project is wrapped by an internal and external double-skin honeycomb motif that also organizes the interior design language. The three-level concourse separates international departures, domestic departures, and arrivals. Sculptural tree-like white elements distribute air-conditioning throughout the terminal.

title: Tianjin Binhai Library / MVRDV + TUPDI
architect: MVRDV; Tianjin Urban Planning and Design Institute (TUPDI)
summary_en: Tianjin Binhai Library is a 33,700 m² cultural centre whose defining interior is a terraced bookshelf landscape wrapped around a luminous spherical auditorium. The building was designed within a strict volume defined by the wider masterplan of the district. Educational spaces line the perimeter across five levels. The project was built to the Chinese Green Star energy-efficiency standard and became widely recognized immediately after opening.

title: House of Music, Budapest / Sou Fujimoto Architects
materials: SentryGlas high-performance laminated glazing by Kuraray
summary_en: House of Music, Budapest is a cultural museum and music venue in City Park. Its floating perforated canopy is shaped in dialogue with the surrounding tree crowns, allowing light to pass through large organic openings. The 9,000 m² building merges exhibition halls, performance spaces, and public outdoor areas under one continuous roof. The project translates the park canopy into an architectural section that blends landscape and institution.

title: Taipei Performing Arts Center / OMA
summary_en: Taipei Performing Arts Center organizes three different theaters around a central cube that consolidates stages, backstages, and support spaces. The building is conceived to be entered and experienced from all sides rather than through a singular monumental front. A public loop lets visitors circulate through the complex regardless of ticket ownership. The project redefines the performing arts center as an open civic machine within the dense urban fabric of Shilin.

title: MahaNakhon Tower / Büro Ole Scheeren
summary_en: MahaNakhon is a 314-metre mixed-use tower that breaks the conventional high-rise silhouette with a spiralling pixelated void carved through its facade. The project dissolves the usual tower-podium typology into a vertically and horizontally connected urban assemblage of tower, podium landscape, cube, and public square. Residential, hospitality, retail, and public observation functions are woven together into one continuous urban section. The facade subtraction becomes both urban identity and a spatial device for terraces, outlooks, and collective programs.
